items.title: Peter Vacher interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001
items.q: I interviewed John Hicks, a terrific piano player about eighteen months

ctx.x: Do you have to balance what you want to write about and what an editor might want you to write about?

I do now. Much more now. We’re very fortunate. In the 60s when I was getting into my stride on all this, Jazz Monthly, Jazz Journal was also at its peak then. I was writing for Coda in Canada. They almost, there was an openness. I don’t remember any editor saying, “Oh I don’t think we want to publish his story.” That is not the position now. I mean for instance I interviewed John Hicks, a terrific piano player about eighteen months

ago — a couple of years ago. I can not place the full story, an as-told-to oral history type piece on John Hicks. Whereas previously I would prepare someone’s life story, an as- told-to, a literally a sort of let’s start at the beginning and right through to where we are now, and I would place those with magazines like Jazz Journal or Jazz Monthly without question. It might run to five thousand words and no one would be bothered, because that’s something that hadn’t been done and it was something that people…
